lines.text: All that separates {leader} from the answer is the season that hasn't happened yet. Lovely pressure, that.
Look at {trailer} now, with a final opportunity to ask a very awkward question of the standings.
Nobody can borrow certainty from yesterday when the deciding season is still waiting to be played.
Right then, {leader} has the advantage, but the only result worth framing is still to come.
Suddenly the arguments sound different. Every prediction must survive the last season before it counts for anything.
Once the whiteboard is wiped, {trailer} has a last chance to change what goes into permanent ink.
lines.was: This is where {trailer} gets a chance to turn a long conversation into a memorable reply.

lines.text: Forget the comfortable chair, {leader}. The last act of this rivalry comes with no reserved seating.
I'd rather see the season played than hear another pundit explain how it's bound to finish.
If you want a rivalry with teeth, this is it. Nobody gets an answer without playing the closer.
lines.was: Credit to both managers for taking this all the way to a conclusion nobody can announce early.

lines.text: Plenty has happened already, but the Showdown has kept its biggest decision for the closing chapter.
Unfashionable thought, perhaps, but {trailer} could yet make the favourite a footnote rather than the headline.
lines.was: Imagine being {trailer}, knowing the door is still open and the next chance is the last.

lines.text: On the studio chalkboard, {leader} occupies the top line. The bottom line hasn't been written.
lines.was: What {leader} has earned is an edge, not permission to skip the decisive part.

lines.text: We have opinions in this studio, naturally. The trouble is the final season hasn't heard them.
Our panel has spent ages circling possibilities. Now that circle has the exact size of one season.
lines.was: Now the rivalry has somewhere precise to go, and nowhere left to hide after it gets there.

lines.text: Listen to the question hanging over {leader}: can the advantage survive the only season remaining?
Naturally, the schedule saved its most inconvenient appointment for last, the one that decides the lot.
lines.was: There's something rather fitting about a competition that refuses to settle itself before the last assignment.

lines.text: For {trailer}, the road ahead is short enough to concentrate the mind and open enough to matter.
I wouldn't book the trophy photographer yet. The camera can wait until the final decision has been earned.
lines.was: An unfinished contest is a dangerous place to act like you've already written the thank-you speech.

lines.text: Every previous season has led {leader} to this position. The next will decide what it's worth.
We've worn grooves in the studio floor arguing. The last campaign will do more than our pacing.
lines.was: Let's see who handles the closing stretch, because the studio has exhausted its supply of confident guesses.

lines.text: The finish is in sight, but neither manager can claim what the last season hasn't awarded.
Give {trailer} a motivational cliché if you must. I'd rather see a season that makes one unnecessary.
lines.was: You could give {trailer} a stirring speech. I'd suggest leaving room for a strong final campaign.

lines.text: In football terms, {leader} has the better starting position. In rivalry terms, we're still listening.
One season remains, and suddenly the smallest decisions feel rather larger than our television set.
I trust {leader} has kept the presentation-case receipt. There remains the small matter of a final campaign.
lines.was: Before anyone orders the presentation case, perhaps {leader} should attend to the business still on the calendar.

lines.text: My favourite thing about {trailer}'s position? The rival can hear the footsteps but can't see the finish.
Could someone unplug the forecast machine? It's had its fun, and the actual contest still has the microphone.
lines.was: Someone pass the studio a fresh prediction. Ours have an irritating habit of meeting actual football.

lines.text: If {leader} wanted peace and quiet, choosing a last-season showdown was a curious way to find it.
Apparently we've reached the part where the pundits become less useful and the managers become more interesting.
Good news for {trailer}, there's still a say in the ending. Bad news for us, no easy forecast.
Put the headline in pencil, please. Ink deserves to wait for a decision the contest hasn't made.
lines.was: Pencil in a verdict if you like. Keep the eraser handy until that remaining season is finished.

lines.text: Tell {leader} the best seat in the house doesn't come with a cushion against a final challenge.
Of course our pundits want closure. They're the only people here paid to sound certain before the evidence arrives.
lines.was: It's almost cruel to make our panel wait for the answer. Almost, because the suspense is excellent.

lines.text: I've heard {trailer} discussed as though the closing credits were already rolling. Someone check the projector.
Well, {leader} can enjoy the view for now. Just don't mistake the balcony for the trophy room.
Anyone who claims this is settled has apparently found a way to play next season in advance.
Interesting position for {trailer}, isn't it? The argument can still be won, but the rehearsal is over.
Picture our panel holding up prediction cards. Not one of them doubles as an entry on the scoreboard.
lines.was: Our experts can pick sides all evening. The last season isn't required to agree with a single one.

lines.text: Fancy being {leader} with an advantage and the knowledge that there's a proper examination to come.
Maybe {trailer} would prefer another dozen opportunities. There is only the final one, and it counts.
Don't offer me a prediction wrapped like a present. The ribbon comes off after the deciding campaign.
Surely {leader} knows the one thing a lead cannot buy, a guarantee about the remaining season.
The wise thing for {trailer} is to see opportunity here, not a deadline dressed as bad news.
It's a rare pleasure to watch the analysts run out of ways to say 'I think' and mean 'I know'.
lines.was: At least we've found the one occasion when the studio's loudest opinion carries absolutely no authority.

lines.text: Could {leader} carry the advantage home? Certainly. Could this rivalry still turn? That's why we're here.
Familiar faces, familiar arguments, and a fresh problem: there's no extra chapter after the one ahead.
I'll say this for {trailer}, the final opportunity arrives with the answer still genuinely in play.
Let the engraver finish their tea. The name won't be decided by who shouts loudest in here.
lines.was: Keep your hands off the commemorative pen. Neither side has signed the ending just yet.

lines.text: There's a full stop waiting at the end of this rivalry. It would be rude to print it early.
lines.was: Most panels would love a neat conclusion. The Showdown insists we watch the remaining football first.

lines.text: Spare a thought for {leader}, whose reward for doing well is one last season under the microscope.
From here the campaign narrows to a single passage, and the whole rivalry must travel through it.
Picture {trailer} at the edge of the final chapter, with every earlier disappointment still answerable.
Here is the peculiar thing about {leader}'s position: so close to the prize, and still far from certainty.
lines.was: There it is, the last open door. {leader} stands nearest the prize, but hasn't crossed the threshold.

lines.text: Everything before this feels like preparation. The unresolved question now has one season in which to speak.
Whichever way it falls, {trailer} can still make the ending worthy of the rivalry that preceded it.
No more future campaigns to soften the outcome. The next season will give this contest its final shape.
Under that studio light, {leader}'s position looks strong. Under the weight of the finale, it remains tested.
A long campaign can hide its sharpest turn in the very last bend. We've reached that bend.
As the final whistle for this whole adventure approaches, the identity of the champion remains unconfirmed.
lines.was: Somewhere beyond the next season is a verdict nobody in this room can honestly deliver tonight.

lines.text: Turn the calendar to its last square, and there is still room for an upset.
lines.was: The margin of possibility has narrowed to one season, yet the question between these managers remains enormous.

lines.text: With {trailer} still able to challenge, the coming campaign matters more than any argument we can stage.
Call it the threshold, not the destination. {leader} still has to see this contest through.
Some campaigns furnish a cabinet. This next one decides which manager gets to close the book.
lines.was: There are seasons you remember for trophies, and seasons you remember because everything depended on them.

lines.text: Just when a rivalry seems to have said enough, it saves the sentence that matters most for last.
Can {trailer} find the answer? The stage is ready, and the final season still has its say.
Every forecast now carries a question mark, because one campaign stands between {leader} and the finish.
Respect the story so far. The closing installment still has power to rearrange the whole shelf.
lines.was: Whatever the earlier story, the closing season gives both managers a chance to define how it's remembered.

lines.text: Being at the front gives {leader} a luxury and a headache: the target is impossible to miss.
lines.was: This is the moment when a healthy advantage becomes a responsibility, as {leader} will discover.

lines.text: Follow the road signs now, and there is no detour left. The final season is the only turn.
lines.was: Nothing about the destination is certain. What is certain is that the road ends after the next campaign.

lines.text: For all the talk surrounding {trailer}, the decisive answer cannot arrive until the season does.
Beyond the next set of results lies either relief or a remarkable reversal. Neither has happened yet.
There is no quieter way to say it: {leader} faces the final test of the whole competition.
If this rivalry were a book, the last page would be the one everybody keeps trying to peek at.
lines.was: If this rivalry were a book, someone has been keeping the last page folded over for years.

lines.text: Standings may favour {leader}, but they cannot describe an ending which hasn't been played.
We've reached the climax without reaching a conclusion. For once, those aren't quite the same thing.
lines.was: How often does a competition reach its conclusion with the outcome still inviting an argument?

lines.text: You have to admire {trailer}'s opportunity. It's awkward, demanding, and infinitely better than a closed door.
Easy for me to say, but {leader} ought to treat this like an assignment, not a victory lap.
Here's a studio wager I can defend: the final season will make at least one of us look foolish.
Take the long view of {trailer}, and there's still a perfectly good reason to believe in a late reply.
Being the favourite is pleasant for {leader}, until you remember that favourites still have to finish.
Sound engineer, save the triumphant sting. We haven't earned the right to choose whose entrance it accompanies.
lines.was: Leave the dramatic music ready, but don't press play until there's a real ending to accompany it.

lines.text: One final campaign, and {trailer} has the chance to replace the current story with a different conclusion.
I'd caution {leader} against collecting congratulations early. Nobody enjoys returning a prematurely polished speech.
In this studio, every pundit has a theory. Out there, the remaining season has the deciding vote.
Consider the difference between a favourite and a champion: a season that still needs playing.
lines.was: No sensible person should confuse a strong position with an outcome, especially at this particular moment.

lines.text: Think of {trailer} as the unanswered question. The season ahead supplies the response, whichever way it goes.
I enjoy a premature verdict as much as any pundit, but this particular one would age terribly.
lines.was: There will be plenty of time for grand judgments once the last installment has actually been completed.

lines.text: I've checked the agenda, and {leader} still has a rather important appointment with the unfinished business.
My cue cards say 'certain winner'. The production team wisely left the name blank.
lines.was: Our confidence is charming, but the next campaign hasn't signed up to follow the panel's script.

lines.text: With the finish so near, {trailer} needs a meaningful response, not an encouraging review from us.
For once the phrase 'all to play for' isn't studio wallpaper. The last season can still alter the verdict.
lines.was: That is the beauty of leaving the decision open, the final season has something genuine to settle.

lines.text: Say what you like about {leader}'s advantage, it cannot be passed directly into the history books.
A season still to play, a whole rivalry still to settle. Even our panel should respect that.
Worth remembering, {trailer} is not being asked to rewrite the past, only to challenge the ending.
I'd frame our predictions if there were anything worth hanging yet. This contest keeps moving the picture.
lines.was: Please don't make the same mistake as our predictions and forget the contest is still alive.

lines.text: The last opportunity is rarely comfortable, and that goes for {leader} as much as anyone else.
As for {trailer}, this is a lovely moment to let ambition do the talking and pundits keep guessing.
On the eve of the ending, the last thing this story needs is a narrator pretending to know it.
lines.was: There's an excellent story in the making here, provided we don't spoil it by declaring a conclusion.

lines.text: Pack the studio notes away. The managers still have a whole season in which to contradict every page.
lines.was: Close the studio notebooks for now. The managers have the only chapter left that can settle this.

lines.text: However loudly we argue, {leader} and {trailer} must let the remaining season supply the answer.
